message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Build

permissions:
  contents: read

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - '*'
  push:
    branches:
      - 'main'
      - 'hotfix-*'

concurrency:
  # On main, we don't want any jobs cancelled.
  # On PR branches, we cancel the job if new commits are pushed.
  group: ${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}

jobs:
  build:
    name: "Build"
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        java-version: [ '17' ]
    env:
      ALLURE_MATRIX_ENV: ubuntu-jdk-${{ matrix.java-version }}
      ALLURE_TEST_DUMP_NAME: allure-results-build-jdk-${{ matrix.java-version }}
      ALLURE_E2E_DUMP_NAME: allure-results-e2e-jdk-${{ matrix.java-version }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20.x'
      - name: Set up JDK ${{ matrix.java-version }}
        uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: 'zulu'
          java-version: ${{ matrix.java-version }}
      - name: Setup Gradle
        uses: gradle/actions/setup-gradle@v6
        with:
          gradle-version: 'wrapper'
      - name: Build without tests
        run: ./gradlew build buildDeb buildRpm -x test
      - name: Test with Allure
        run: npx -y allure@3 run --config ./allurerc.mjs --rerun 2 --environment="${{ env.ALLURE_MATRIX_ENV }}" --dump="${{ env.ALLURE_TEST_DUMP_NAME }}" -- ./gradlew test
      - name: Install Playwright browser
        run: cd allure-generator && npx playwright install --with-deps chromium
      - name: Run Playwright e2e with Allure
        run: npx -y allure@3 run --config ./allurerc.mjs --rerun 2 --environment="${{ env.ALLURE_MATRIX_ENV }}" --dump="${{ env.ALLURE_E2E_DUMP_NAME }}" -- ./gradlew :allure-generator:testE2E
      - name: Upload allure-commandline artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: allure-commandline
          path: allure-commandline/build/install/allure-commandline
      - name: Upload Allure test dump
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: ${{ env.ALLURE_TEST_DUMP_NAME }}
          path: ./${{ env.ALLURE_TEST_DUMP_NAME }}.zip
      - name: Upload Allure e2e dump
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: ${{ env.ALLURE_E2E_DUMP_NAME }}
          path: ./${{ env.ALLURE_E2E_DUMP_NAME }}.zip
      - name: Upload testcmd smoke results artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: testcmd-smoke-results
          path: allure-generator/tests/fixtures/raw/commandline-smoke
  testcmd:
    name: "Test Allure Commandline"
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    needs: build
    env:
      ALLURE_TESTCMD_DUMP_NAME: allure-results-testcmd-${{ matrix.os }}-jdk-${{ matrix.java-version }}-${{ matrix.install.name }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: true
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, windows-latest]
        java-version: [ '8', '11', '17', '20' ]
        install:
          - name: regular
            path: .
          - name: nested
            path: testcmd/install/allure-commandline-under-a-nested-working-directory/with-windows-launcher-classpath-length-regression/allure-commandline
    steps:
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20.x'
      - name: Set up JRE ${{ matrix.java-version }}
        uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          java-package: 'jre'
          distribution: 'zulu'
          java-version: ${{ matrix.java-version }}
      - name: Download allure-commandline artifact
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          name: allure-commandline
          path: ${{ matrix.install.path }}
      - name: Download testcmd smoke results artifact
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          name: testcmd-smoke-results
          path: testcmd-smoke-results
      - name: Add execute permissions to script
        run: chmod +x ${{ matrix.install.path }}/bin/allure
      - name: Run version command
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $allure = '${{ matrix.install.path }}/bin/allure'
          npx -y allure@3 check `
            --name 'testcmd allure --version (${{ matrix.os }}, Java ${{ matrix.java-version }}, ${{ matrix.install.name }})' `
            --tag testcmd `
            --tag ${{ matrix.os }} `
            --tag java-${{ matrix.java-version }} `
            --tag ${{ matrix.install.name }} `
            --dump '${{ env.ALLURE_TESTCMD_DUMP_NAME }}-version' `
            -- pwsh -NoProfile -Command "& '$allure' --version"
      - name: Generate demo report
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $allure = '${{ matrix.install.path }}/bin/allure'
          npx -y allure@3 check `
            --name 'testcmd allure generate (${{ matrix.os }}, Java ${{ matrix.java-version }}, ${{ matrix.install.name }})' `
            --tag testcmd `
            --tag ${{ matrix.os }} `
            --tag java-${{ matrix.java-version }} `
            --tag ${{ matrix.install.name }} `
            --dump '${{ env.ALLURE_TESTCMD_DUMP_NAME }}-generate' `
            -- pwsh -NoProfile -Command "& '$allure' generate testcmd-smoke-results"
      - name: Verify generated tree data
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $requiredFiles = @(
            'allure-report/data/behaviors.json',
            'allure-report/data/behaviors.csv',
            'allure-report/data/packages.json',
            'allure-report/widgets/behaviors.json'
          )

          $missingFiles = $requiredFiles | Where-Object {
            -not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $_ -PathType Leaf)
          }

          if ($missingFiles.Count -gt 0) {
            $message = "Missing generated report files: $($missingFiles -join ', ')"
            npx -y allure@3 check `
              --name 'testcmd generated tree data (${{ matrix.os }}, Java ${{ matrix.java-version }}, ${{ matrix.install.name }})' `
              --status failed `
              --message $message `
              --tag testcmd `
              --tag ${{ matrix.os }} `
              --tag java-${{ matrix.java-version }} `
              --tag ${{ matrix.install.name }} `
              --dump '${{ env.ALLURE_TESTCMD_DUMP_NAME }}-tree-data'
            Write-Error $message
            exit 1
          }

          $requiredFiles | ForEach-Object {
            Write-Host "Verified $_"
          }

          $message = "Verified generated report files: $($requiredFiles -join ', ')"
          npx -y allure@3 check `
            --name 'testcmd generated tree data (${{ matrix.os }}, Java ${{ matrix.java-version }}, ${{ matrix.install.name }})' `
            --status passed `
            --message $message `
            --tag testcmd `
            --tag ${{ matrix.os }} `
            --tag java-${{ matrix.java-version }} `
            --tag ${{ matrix.install.name }} `
            --dump '${{ env.ALLURE_TESTCMD_DUMP_NAME }}-tree-data'
      - name: Upload Allure testcmd dump
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: ${{ env.ALLURE_TESTCMD_DUMP_NAME }}
          path: ./${{ env.ALLURE_TESTCMD_DUMP_NAME }}-*.zip
          if-no-files-found: ignore
  report:
    needs: [build, testcmd]
    name: "Build report"
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: always()
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: write
      checks: write
    env:
      ALLURE_SERVICE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.ALLURE_SERVICE_TOKEN }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '20.x'
      - name: Download Allure dumps
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          pattern: allure-results-*
          path: ./
          merge-multiple: true
      - name: Generate Allure report
        run: npx -y allure@3 generate --config ./allurerc.mjs --dump="allure-results-*.zip" --output=./build/allure-report
      - name: Post Allure summary
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork == false
        uses: allure-framework/allure-action@v0
        with:
          report-directory: ./build/allure-report
          github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}",
  "rationale": "The testcmd job runs a 16-cell matrix (2 OS x 4 Java versions x 2 install paths) with fail-fast: false, so every cell runs to completion even after a failure. The P-LIT-FAIL-FAST pattern (cancel remaining matrix jobs after failure) is supported by experiment records with scenario_passed outcomes. Setting fail-fast: true on the testcmd matrix cancels in-flight sibling cells when one fails, saving CI resources while still reporting the failure. The build job has a single-element matrix so fail-fast is irrelevant there. No permissions, secrets, or deployment steps are changed, and all build/test steps are preserved.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-scenario-three-run-4bb0552aeb09c242", "experiment:batch-scenario-three-run-b6e04fef7ef24997"]
}

The user wants me to propose a CI optimization for the given workflow, based on evidence. Let me analyze the workflow and the evidence.

The workflow is a GitHub Actions workflow for building and testing an Allure Report project. It has:
1. `build` job - builds with Gradle, runs tests with Allure, runs Playwright e2e tests
2. `testcmd` job - tests Allure Commandline on multiple OS/Java versions (matrix)
3. `report` job - generates Allure report

Key observations:
- The `build` job has `fail-fast: false` with a single-element matrix (java-version: ['17'])
- The `testcmd` job has `fail-fast: false` with a matrix of os × java-version × install (2 × 4 × 2 = 16 combinations)
- There's concurrency control that cancels in-progress jobs on PR branches but not on main

Evidence patterns that could apply:
1. P-LIT-FAIL-FAST: "Cancel remaining matrix jobs after failure" - The `testcmd` job has a matrix with fail-fast: false. Setting fail-fast: true would cancel remaining matrix jobs when one fails. This saves CI resources. The evidence shows this pattern with measured/synthetic results. The contraindications are "Every matrix outcome is required" and "Full failure diagnostics are required". For a testcmd job, if one matrix cell fails, do we need all others? Probably not - it's testing the same commandline tool across different environments. If one fails, we likely want to know but don't necessarily need all 16 to complete. However, the contraindication says "Every matrix outcome is required" - we need to check if this applies.

Looking at the workflow, the `testcmd` job tests Allure Commandline across different OS/Java versions. These are independent test combinations. If one fails, the others are still valuable for understanding compatibility. But the pattern says to evaluate the contract before changing cancellation.

2. P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT: "Bound jobs with a custom timeout" - The workflow has no explicit timeout-minutes on jobs. Adding timeouts could prevent runaway consumption. The evidence shows this pattern with measured results (26.8% savings in one experiment). The contraindication is "Valid slow runs exceed the proposed limit".

3. P-LIT-GHA-CACHE: "Cache dependency downloads" - The workflow uses npm ci, setup-java, gradle wrapper, playwright install. These could benefit from caching. But the evidence says "Examples are illustrative pseudocode, not measured patches" and the evidence scope is literature report.

Let me think about which optimization is best supported:

P-LIT-FAIL-FAST seems most directly applicable. The `testcmd` job has a matrix with `fail-fast: false`. Changing to `fail-fast: true` would cancel remaining matrix jobs when one fails. This is a minimal change that preserves coverage (all matrix cells still run unless one fails, in which case remaining are cancelled - but the failure is still reported).

Wait, but the contraindication says "Every matrix outcome is required". For the testcmd job, are all matrix outcomes required? It's testing compatibility across OS/Java versions. If one fails, we might still want to know about others. But typically in CI, fail-fast: true is acceptable for matrix jobs where you want quick feedback.

Actually, looking more carefully at the evidence:
- P-LIT-FAIL-FAST has evidence from synthetic experiments (scenario_passed)
- The pattern says "Matrix cancellation saves remaining work"
- Preconditions: "Matrix failure makes remaining results dispensable under an explicit study policy"

The `build` job has a single-element matrix, so fail-fast doesn't matter there. The `testcmd` job has a 16-cell matrix. Setting fail-fast: true there would save resources when a failure occurs.

But wait - I need to check if there's a more concrete, measured evidence. The P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT has a measured_ci_workflow_on_fork evidence with 26.82% elapsed savings. But that was for adding a timeout-minutes: 5 to a job that was completing in ~34 seconds. The jobs in this workflow are likely much longer (Gradle build, Playwright tests), so a 5-minute timeout would be too aggressive and could break valid runs.

Let me reconsider P-LIT-FAIL-FAST. The evidence shows:
- Pattern: P-LIT-FAIL-FAST
- Evidence IDs: experiment:batch-scenario-three-run-4bb0552aeb09c242, experiment:batch-scenario-three-run-b6e04fef7ef24997
- These are synthetic but show scenario_passed
- The change is setting fail-fast: true on a matrix strategy

This seems like a good fit. The `testcmd` job has `fail-fast: false` with a multi-cell matrix. Changing to `fail-fast: true` is a minimal, safe change that preserves all test coverage when everything passes, and cancels remaining (redundant) jobs when one fails.

Actually, let me also consider the `build` job. It has `fail-fast: false` but only one matrix element, so it doesn't matter.

For `testcmd`, the matrix is:
- os: [ubuntu-latest, windows-latest]
- java-version: ['8', '11', '17', '20']
- install: [regular, nested]

That's 16 combinations. If one fails early, the other 15 would still run with fail-fast: false. With fail-fast: true, they'd be cancelled.

Is there any contraindication? "Every matrix outcome is required" - for compatibility testing, you might argue all outcomes are needed. But the pattern says to evaluate the contract. Since this is a testcmd job (testing the commandline tool), and the build job already runs the main tests, the testcmd is additional compatibility testing. If one environment fails, knowing that is sufficient to flag an issue; running all 16 may not be necessary.

However, I need to be careful. The instructions say "Preserve the intended build and test coverage". With fail-fast: true, if one cell fails, other cells are cancelled - so we lose coverage on those cells for that run. But the failure itself is still captured. This is the standard trade-off of fail-fast.

Let me look at whether there's stronger evidence. The P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT has measured_ci_workflow_on_fork evidence with actual savings. But applying a custom timeout to this workflow is risky because:
- The build job runs Gradle build, tests, Playwright e2e - could take 10+ minutes
- The testcmd job runs on Windows and Ubuntu with multiple Java versions
- Without knowing typical durations, setting a timeout could break valid runs

The P-LIT-FAIL-FAST evidence is synthetic but directly applicable to the matrix strategy in this workflow.

Change the `testcmd` job's strategy from `fail-fast: false` to `fail-fast: true`.

- actions/setup-node@v7 with cache: npm
- actions/setup-java@v6
- gradle/actions/setup-gradle@v6
- npx -y allure@3
- npx playwright install --with-deps chromium

The setup-node already has cache: npm. But Gradle dependencies and Playwright browsers aren't cached. However, the P-LIT-GHA-CACHE evidence is from literature (not measured on this repo) and says "Examples are illustrative pseudocode, not measured patches." Also, adding caching requires more complex changes and could affect correctness if not done properly.

I think the cleanest, most evidence-supported change is P-LIT-FAIL-FAST on the testcmd job.

```yaml
    ...

      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
```
to:

Everything else stays the same.

Let me use both or just one. The instructions say "APPLY requires at least one" evidence ID. I'll use one or both.

Let me write out the complete updated workflow YAML.

For the testcmd job: it's testing Allure Commandline across different OS/Java versions. These are compatibility tests. If the tool fails on Windows with Java 8, do we need to know if it also fails on Ubuntu with Java 20? Probably yes for full compatibility matrix. But the pattern explicitly says to "Evaluate the contract before changing cancellation" and "Record canceled jobs". 

The question is whether this repository requires all matrix outcomes. Looking at the required_checks in the repository context: `"names": [], "status": "not_verified"`. So there are no explicitly required checks listed. The workflow itself doesn't indicate that all matrix cells are required.
